claim: Dénia Castle costs EUR 3 adult / EUR 2 students-seniors / EUR 1 children 8-16 (under 8 and residents free); sits 60m on a hilltop with panoramic Mediterranean views; pedestrian-only access; ~2-3 hour visit.
quote: Adults: €3 ... Students/Seniors/Groups (25+): €2 ... Children (8–16): €1 ... Under 8: Free ... The 60-meter hilltop location offers panoramic vistas of Dénia.

claim: The Dénia Archaeological Museum relocated from the castle to Casa de la Marquesa (Calle Cavallers 3) downtown in October 2024, admission is free, and it covers four periods: Iberian, Roman (Dianium), Islamic (Taifa of Daniya) and Christian (13th-18th c.).
quote: The museum relocated to Casa de la Marquesa (Calle Cavallers, 3) in October 2024 ... Entrance to the Archaeological Museum is free ... Iberian ... Roman ... Islamic ... Christian

claim: Les Roques is the old quarter preserving the Arab medina with narrow pedestrian streets and is the gateway to the castle; Loreto Street is the most emblematic pedestrian thoroughfare, dense with restaurants and tapas bars.
quote: the Les Roques neighborhood, described as preserving "the essence of the Arab medina" ... Loreto Street stands as the most emblematic thoroughfare, completely pedestrianized ... high concentration of restaurants and tapas bars

claim: Cova de l'Aigua sits on Montgó's north face at ~350m; the PR-CV 152 trail from Ermita del Pare Pere runs 30-45 minutes one-way and the cave (two rooms, a pond, a 238 AD Roman inscription) was used from Iberian times and as an Arab Taifa-era water store.
quote: on the north face of Montgó, about 350 meters high ... PR-CV 152 trail ... lasts between 30 and 45 minutes ... At the entrance there is a Roman inscription dating from 238 AD ... two rooms and a small pond at the bottom

claim: The Cova de l'Aigua circular hike is rated difficult, about 6.15 km / 3.8 miles, taking roughly 2h33m, with some technical and hazardous terrain.
quote: The Cova de l'Aigua - Racó del Bou Trail is a difficult 3.8-mile hike ... the total distance is 6.15 km with an estimated time of 2 hours 33 minutes ... highly technical, difficult, or hazardous terrain

claim: The Cabo de San Antonio lighthouse (built 1861, 17m tall, 175m above sea level) sits where Montgó plunges into the sea on 150m+ cliffs; the adjacent mirador overlooks Xàbia bay and on clear days you can see Ibiza, reached via CV-736 / Carretera del Faro (~4km).
quote: Located 175 metres above sea level, its current construction dates back to 1861 ... 17 meters high ... cliffs of more than 150 meters ... you can see the island of Ibiza when the day is very clear ... about 4km to the lighthouse

claim: Les Rotes is the southern rocky coastline mixing pine and sea, ending at Les Arenetes beach, while Montgó Natural Park is an iconic regional landmark with multi-difficulty hiking routes between Dénia and Jávea.
quote: Les Rotes Coastal Area ... "pinos y casitas de campo" ... Les Arenetes Beach marks the area's end ... Montgó Natural Park ... "todo un icono para la comarca"

claim: Dénia has over 20 km of coastline split into Les Marines (north of the port, long fine-sand beaches) and Les Rotes (south, rocky coves with clear water ideal for diving).
quote: Les Marines, north of the port, with long, fine sandy beaches, and Les Rotes, to the south, where rocky coves and crystal-clear waters dominate, ideal for diving.

claim: Dénia holds 7 Blue Flag beaches for 2025-2026: six sandy Les Marines beaches (Punta del Raset, Les Albaranes, Les Marines, Les Bovetes, Els Molins, Les Deveses) plus the rocky Punta Negra cove in Les Rotes, which won its first Blue Flag in 2025.
quote: Punta Negra - Rocky cove newly awarded in 2025, described as 'a natural swimming pool' with 'crystal-clear waters' and marine reserve location

claim: Les Marines beach (including Blay Beach and Las Brisas) is sandy, family-friendly, holds a renewed Blue Flag, and is lifeguarded by the Red Cross in summer with foot showers, sunbed rental, children's play areas and nearby parking.
quote: Les Marines (including Blay Beach and Las Brisas) boasts a Blue Flag for water quality and service guarantee renewed for 2025.

claim: Les Deveses is Dénia's widest sandy beach at nearly 3 km, sits at km 10.8 (~12 km, the furthest from the centre), was fully regenerated in 2024, flies a Blue Flag, and is renowned for windsurfing, kitesurfing and wingfoiling thanks to thermal winds.
quote: Les Deveses extends nearly 3 kilometers and represents 'the widest sandy beach in the municipality of Dénia.' ... Renowned for windsurfing, kitesurfing, and wingfoiling due to thermal winds

claim: Les Rotes coves south of town suit snorkelling: El Trampolí has flat rock platforms and a wooden diving board within the marine reserve, Les Arenetes offers rock formations and kayak routes, and La Cala is a 100% natural rock nudist cove with no services reached via a cliff path.
quote: El Trampolí ... Flat rock and large natural platforms ... Wooden diving platform, lifeguard in summer ... La Cala ... 100% natural rock nudist beach, without commercial services

claim: Les Rotes lies about 1.5 km from Dénia town centre and its rocky seabed within the Cabo de San Antonio marine reserve is rich in fish and marine life, making it the prime area for snorkelling, diving and tranquil secluded coves rather than sandy sunbathing.
quote: Les Rotes is located approximately 1.5 km from the town center and consists of a beach of rocky coves ... The seabed here is rich in marine life ... a delight for divers and snorkelers alike.

claim: Punta Negra is a roughly 1,400 m rocky cove in Les Rotes that received its first Blue Flag in 2025 and is among Dénia's most popular snorkelling and diving spots within the Cabo de San Antonio Marine Reserve.
quote: This rocky cove, stretching for about 1,400 meters, is one of the most beautiful and beloved in Dénia. In 2025, the beach received its first Blue flag

claim: The Montgó summit hike via the PR-CV 355 trail from the Dénia shooting range climbs to 753m, takes roughly 3-5 hours round trip, and is rated difficult with an exposed final ridge scramble.
quote: The ascent usually takes between three to five hours round trip... summit itself at 753m... final section involves a thrilling scramble along the summit ridge where you will need to use your hands.

claim: The Montgó summit route is the most difficult of the area's trails with over 600m of steep rocky ascent, unsuitable for those with vertigo and to be avoided in storms, fog or high heat as there is no refuge.
quote: steep ascent of over 600 meters on rocky terrain and a final scramble along an exposed ridge... not suitable for those with vertigo. Refrain from climbing Montgó when there is a risk of thunderstorms, fog or high temperatures.

claim: Cova Tallada access is regulated in 2026 from March 28-April 13, April 28-May 5, and continuously June 15-October 15; outside those dates no permit is needed.
quote: access to Cueva Tallada is regulated from March 28 to April 13 (both inclusive); from April 28 to May 5 (both inclusive); and from June 15 to October 15 (both inclusive).

claim: The free Cova Tallada reservation is made online in the Generalitat Valenciana Reservation Manager, valid for max 5 people, bookable only 10 days in advance, with a 90-minute maximum stay in the cave.
quote: reservation for visiting Cova Tallada is made online in the Reservation Manager of the Generalitat Valenciana. Each reservation is valid for a maximum of 5 people. Reservations can only be made 10 days in advance... maximum stay in the cave is 1 hour and 30 minutes

claim: Cova Tallada daily limits are 370 hikers and 112 kayakers with max 71 people in the cave at once, and unauthorized entry carries a 601 euro fine.
quote: maximum of 71 hikers at any one time. Daily limits are 370 hikers and 112 kayakers... Unauthorized entry comes with a fine of 601 euros.

claim: The on-foot walk to Cova Tallada is about 1.5 km each way, takes 45-60 minutes, and is high difficulty due to steep slopes and slippery rocky areas.
quote: approximately 1.5 km (one way)... 45 to 60 minutes... High difficulty due to steep slopes and slippery rocky areas.

claim: A guided kayak-and-snorkel excursion to Cova Tallada costs about 50 euros per person, lasts roughly 2.5 hours over a 4km round trip, departs from the Mena Restaurant car park at the end of Les Rotes, and includes kayak, wetsuit and guide.
quote: Approximately 2.5 hours total... €50 per person... Departure Point: Parking lot adjacent to Mena Restaurant at the end of Las Rotas road in Dénia... Kayak and life jacket... Neoprene wetsuit and diving goggles... Professional guide services

claim: Accessing Cova Tallada by kayak through an authorized company does not require a separate reservation; rental packages include life jacket, paddles, kayak, snorkelling gear and insurance.
quote: If you want to access the cave by kayak through one of the authorized companies, you do not need to make a reservation... Kayak rental packages include life jacket, paddles, kayak, snorkeling gear, liability and accident insurance.

claim: Snorkelling and diving around Dénia centre on the Cabo de San Antonio Marine Reserve, a protected area with clear shallow water, colourful fish, octopuses and sea turtles; Aigua Dolç cove at the far end of Les Rotes lies within the reserve.
quote: Marine Reserve of Cabo de San Antonio is a protected area teeming with marine life including colourful fish, octopuses, and sea turtles... Aigua Dolç cove is located at the far end of Les Rotes and within the Cape San Antonio Marine Reserve

claim: The Les Rotes promenade runs almost 3 km from Marineta Casiana beach to Arenetes beach, is pedestrianised for 90% of its length, and is suited to walking, jogging and cycling with bars and restaurants along the way.
quote: distance of almost 3 kilometers along the seashore... starts at the Marineta Casiana beach... ends at the Arenetes beach... runs next to the sea by a pedestrianized place in 90% of its route.

claim: Cycling from Dénia includes the low-difficulty Vía Verde greenway following the old railway line between Dénia and El Verger, plus the flat Les Bassetes Park route of about 3.3 km ideal for children.
quote: Green Way (Vía Verde): A low difficulty route that runs between Denia and El Verger by the old route of the railway... Les Bassetes Park... approximately 3.3 kilometers.

claim: Dénia's red prawn is caught at ~600m depth between Cape San Antonio and Ibiza, is scarce (one or two boxes per boat per day), best boiled in its own seawater for ~3 minutes with no sauce, and costs roughly €150-170/kg at origin.
quote: no more than one or two boxes of Dénia Red Shrimp to the port each day... boiled in her own seawater and without adding any sauces or garnish... prices range between 150 and 170 euros per kilogram

claim: The Mercat Municipal on Magallanes Street (parallel to Marqués de Campo) opens Monday-Saturday 8:00-15:00, has occupied the site since 1954, and houses a fishmonger nave plus bars and cafés (Bar Magallanes, Viciano Bar, Bonanza Bar) for tapas and wine while shopping.
quote: Monday to Saturday, 8:00 AM to 3:00 PM... Located on Magallanes Street... parallel to Calle Marques de Campo... Five bars and cafés (Bar Magallanes, Viciano Bar, Bonanza Bar)

claim: Dénia was designated a UNESCO Creative City of Gastronomy in 2015, valuing local produce (red shrimp, fresh fish, cocas), sustainability and traditional knowledge, with a local Bancalet seal certifying proximity origin.
quote: values the quality of its cuisine, but also its commitment to sustainability, innovation and the transmission of gastronomic knowledge... Bancalet... a declaration of love for the product of proximity

claim: Arròs a banda originated with Alicante fishermen who used low-value fish to make an intense stock in which rice was then cooked, the rice traditionally served separately ('a banda') from the fish.
quote: originated with the fishermen of Alicante, who sold off their best fish and kept the leftovers for stock, in which rice was cooked

claim: Dénia rice specialists for arròs a banda and seafood rice include El Pegolí (classic arròs a banda, since 1943), Casa Federico (over twenty rice varieties), Haití (choose your socarrat level), and Restaurante Mena on the Les Rotes cliffs.
quote: El Pegolí has been living history since 1943, and its classic arròs a banda is essential... Haití allows you to choose the level of socarrat... Restaurante Mena is perched on the cliffs

claim: Dénia hosts an annual International Creative Cuisine Competition of the Dénia Red Prawn, which draws chefs from across Spain and reinforces the city's gastronomic profile.
quote: The red prawn once again challenges culinary creativity in Dénia with a new edition of its International Competition

claim: Jávea (Xàbia) is Dénia's neighbour on the other side of the Montgó mountain with three areas (Old Town, Port, Arenal beach), and a return ferry runs from Dénia to Jávea port for around £10 adult.
quote: Javea is the neighbouring town to Denia on the other side of the Montgo mountain... The Old Town, Javea Port, and the Arenal beach. You can take a return ferry directly from Denia to Javea port

claim: Jávea to Dénia is about a 18-minute drive over a road distance of roughly 12 km.
quote: Javea to Denia takes approximately 18 minutes by car... road distance of 7.6 miles

claim: The Mirador del Cap de Sant Antoni is free to enter with free parking and is accessible 24/7, with views over Dénia, the Gulf of Valencia and Jávea's bay.
quote: Entry to the Mirador del Cap de Sant Antoni is completely free with no admission fee... Free parking is available... accessible 24/7

claim: Cap de la Nau offers dramatic cliffs, an octagonal lighthouse (20 m, ~122 m above sea level) and the boat-accessible Cova dels Òrgans sea cave, with Ibiza visible on clear days.
quote: octagonal lighthouse is 20 meters high and located approximately 122 meters above sea level... Cova dels Organs is a remote marine cave with stalactites... potential sightings of Ibiza on clear days

claim: Calpe is dominated by the Peñón de Ifach, a 332 m limestone rock; the summit hike is a roughly 5 km out-and-back taking 2.5-4 hours round trip.
quote: towering limestone rock rising 332 meters above the sea... round trip usually lasts anywhere from 2.5 to 4 hours... a 5.0-km out-and-back trail

claim: Hiking the Peñón de Ifach requires a free permit booked online in advance, with the natural park capped at 300 visitors per day and reservations openable up to 10 days ahead.
quote: you need a permit, though there's no charge. However, only 300 people are allowed in the nature reserve each day... apply for a hiking permit up to 10 days before

claim: Calpe to Dénia is about 22 km straight-line, roughly 34 km / a half-hour by road.
quote: Distance between Calp and Denia is 22 kilometers (14 miles). The driving distance from Calp to Denia is 34 kilometers (21 miles)

claim: Guadalest (medieval castle village) is about one hour's drive from Dénia, with the Fonts d'Algar waterfalls a further ~30 minutes; the combined organised day tour runs around 7.5 hours.
quote: drive from Denia to Guadalest takes about one hour... Fonts d'Algar, about 30 minutes away... approximately 7.5 hours

claim: The Jalón (Xaló) Valley / Vall de Pop wine country lies along the Gorgos/Jalón river between Jávea and Calpe, less than 30 minutes from Dénia, Xàbia and Calpe, known for sweet Moscatel wines.
quote: part of the Vall de Pop, a valley... that runs along the Gorgos River, also known as the Jalon River. The area is less than 30 minutes from the tourist centers of the region: Denia, Xabia, Calpe

claim: Bodegas Xaló in the Jalón Valley offers guided cellar tours with wine tasting and tapas in the Vall de Pop for groups of 4 to 100 people, around 10 euros per person.
quote: guided tour and tasting in the heart of the Vall del Pop. Guided tours are from 4 and up to 100 people and for a mere 10 euros you can visit the bodega, taste the wines, enjoy some tapas and a free gift

claim: Baleària operates high-speed ferries from Dénia to Ibiza with the fastest crossing at 2 h 15 min (up to ~3 h 15 min depending on vessel/weather), typically 1 daily crossing year-round.
quote: between 2 and 3 h 15 min, with the fastest crossing at 2 hr 15 min... All ferries on this route are high-speed vessels operated by Balearia... 1 daily crossing

claim: Baleària's official Dénia-Ibiza route page is the booking source for current 2026 schedules and fares.
quote: Ferry from Denia to Ibiza | Balearia

claim: Baleària also runs a Dénia-Formentera crossing of roughly 2-3 hours with up to 3 daily departures in summer.
quote: Denia Formentera ferry from 50€... up to 3 daily departures in summer

claim: Driving from Alicante airport (ALC) to Dénia takes about 1h7m (106 km) and from Valencia airport about 1h20m (113 km) via the AP-7 motorway.
quote: It takes around 70 minutes to drive from Alicante Airport to Denia on the AP-7 coastal motorway... Driving from Valencia Airport to Denia takes around 1 hour and 20 minutes via the AP-7 motorway.

claim: TRAM Line 9 (Benidorm–Dénia), the modernized successor to the original 1914–15 FGV narrow-gauge railway, is fully operational since its January 2023 upgrade with Stadler dual-mode trains; Alicante–Dénia requires a Benidorm transfer and takes roughly 3 hours total.
quote: In January 2023, modernization of Line 9 (Benidorm–Dénia) was completed... To reach Dénia from central Alicante... Take Lines 1–4 from Luceros to Benidorm Intermodal station... Transfer to Line 9... Total travel time: Approximately 3 hours

claim: Line 9 runs roughly hourly from about 05:50 to 20:50, with the last Dénia departure connecting toward Alicante leaving around 19:50.
quote: Line 9 (Benidorm–Dénia) runs about once per hour from 05:50 to 20:50, with the last train from Dénia that connects to Alicante leaving around 19:50.

claim: The Festa Major de Dénia 2026 (Santíssima Sang) runs July 3–12, 2026, with Bous a la Mar bull-running sessions at the port bullring from 7:30–9:00 PM on July 4, 5, 6, 7, 8 and 10.
quote: The Festa Major runs from Friday, July 3 through Sunday, July 12, 2026... Saturday, July 4 – 7:30 PM to 9:00 PM... All sessions take place at the bullring in the port area.

claim: Summer traffic restrictions make town-centre parking difficult; visitors are advised to use perimeter car parks like La Vía or Torrecremada and walk into the largely pedestrianized centre, with four free La Marina car parks (250 spaces) near the marina.
quote: During summer months, traffic restrictions in the town centre make parking a real challenge... use perimeter public parking lots, such as La Vía or Torrecremada... four free car parks at La Marina de Dénia with 250 spaces

claim: Dénia has sensorized 277 regulated parking spaces around the Municipal Market and historic centre, with availability shown in real time via the free Park Time app.
quote: 277 regulated parking spaces have been sensorized in streets around the Municipal Market and historic center... Citizens have access to the free mobile application Park Time, which displays the availability of monitored spaces in real time.

claim: Dénia's best months are May, June and September (warm, sunny, fewer crowds); it has a mild microclimate between Montgó mountain and the sea with over 300 sunny days a year, while summer is hottest and busiest.
quote: The best time to visit Dénia is usually late spring and early autumn, especially May, June, and September... a mild, stable and sunny microclimate nestled between Montgó mountain and the Mediterranean, with over 300 days of sunshine a year.

claim: ALSA runs 16+ daily buses Valencia–Dénia and 15+ daily Alicante–Dénia, giving a no-car option from both gateway cities.
quote: ALSA has more than 16 daily bus services between Valencia and Dénia... ALSA has more than 15 daily bus services between Alicante and Dénia.
